text: On the fifteenth day of the second month after they had left the land of Egypt (land of bondage), the whole congregation of Israel (he wrestles with God) set out from Elim (palms) and came to the Desert of Sin (thorn), which is between Elim and Sinai (thorny).
And there in the desert the whole congregation of Israel (he wrestles with God) grumbled against Moses (drawn out) and Aaron (light bringer).

“If only we had died by the LORD’s {YHWH} hand in the land of Egypt (land of bondage)!” they said (he wrestles with God). “There we sat by pots of meat and ate our fill of bread, but you⁺ have brought us into this desert to starve this whole assembly to death!”

Then the LORD {YHWH} said to Moses (drawn out), “Behold, I will rain down bread from heaven for you⁺. Each day the people are to go out and gather enough for that day. In this way I will test whether or not they will follow My instructions.
Then on the sixth day, when they prepare what they bring in, it will be twice as much as they gather on the other days.”

So Moses (drawn out) and Aaron (light bringer) said to all the Israelites (God prevails), “This evening you⁺ will know that it was the LORD {YHWH} who brought you⁺ out of the land of Egypt (land of bondage),
and in the morning you⁺ will see the LORD’s {YHWH} glory, because He has heard your⁺ grumbling against Him. For who are we, that you⁺ should grumble against us?”

And Moses (drawn out) added, “The LORD {YHWH} will give you⁺ meat to eat this evening and bread to fill you in the morning, for He has heard your⁺ grumbling against Him. Who are we? Your⁺ grumblings are not against us but against the LORD.”
Then Moses (drawn out) said to Aaron (light bringer), “Tell the whole congregation of Israel (he wrestles with God), ‘Come before the LORD {YHWH}, for He has heard your⁺ grumbling.’”
And as Aaron (light bringer) was speaking to the whole congregation of Israel (he wrestles with God), they looked toward the desert, and there in a cloud the glory of the LORD {YHWH} appeared.
Then the LORD {YHWH} said to Moses (drawn out),

“I have heard the grumbling of the Israelites (God prevails). Tell them, ‘At twilight \between the two evenings/ you⁺ will eat meat, and in the morning you⁺ will be filled with bread. Then you⁺ will know that I am the LORD your⁺ God {YHWH Eloheikem}.’”
That evening quail came and covered the camp, and in the morning there was a layer of dew around the camp.
When the layer of dew had evaporated, there were thin flakes on the desert floor, as fine as frost on the ground.

When the Israelites (God prevails) saw it, they asked one another, “What is it?” For they did not know what it was. So Moses (drawn out) told them, “It is the bread that the LORD {YHWH} has given you⁺ to eat.
This is what the LORD {YHWH} has commanded: ‘Each one is to gather as much as he needs. You⁺ may take an omer <2 qt / 2.2 l> for each person in your⁺ tent.’”
So the Israelites (God prevails) did this. Some gathered more, and some less.
When they measured it by the omer, he who gathered much had no excess, and he who gathered little had no shortfall <2Co 8:15>. Each one gathered as much as he needed to eat.
Then Moses (drawn out) said to them, “No one may keep any of it until morning.”
But they did not listen to Moses (drawn out); some people left part of it until morning, and it became infested with maggots and began to smell. So Moses was angry with them.
Every morning each one gathered as much as was needed, and when the sun grew hot, it melted away.
On the sixth day, they gathered twice as much food—two omers per person <4 qt / 4.4 l> and all the leaders of the congregation came and reported this to Moses (drawn out).

He told them, “This is what the LORD {YHWH} has said: ‘Tomorrow is to be a day of complete rest, a holy Sabbath to the LORD. So bake what you⁺ want to bake, and boil what you⁺ want to boil. Then set aside whatever remains and keep it until morning.’”
So they set it aside until morning as Moses (drawn out) had commanded, and it did not smell or contain any maggots.
“Eat it today,” Moses (drawn out) said, “because today is a Sabbath to the LORD {YHWH}. Today you⁺ will not find anything in the field.
For six days you⁺ may gather, but on the seventh day, the Sabbath, it will not be there.”
Yet on the seventh day some of the people went out to gather, but they did not find anything.
Then the LORD {YHWH} said to Moses (drawn out), “How long will you⁺ refuse to keep My commandments and instructions?

Understand that the LORD {YHWH} has given you⁺ the Sabbath; that is why on the sixth day He will give you⁺ bread for two days. On the seventh day, everyone must stay where he is; no one may leave his place.”
So the people rested on the seventh day.
Now the house of Israel (he wrestles with God) called the bread manna (What is it?). It was white like coriander seed and tasted like wafers made with honey.

Moses (drawn out) said, “This is what the LORD {YHWH} has commanded: ‘Keep an omer of manna for the generations to come, so that they may see the bread I fed you⁺ in the wilderness when I brought you⁺ out of the land of Egypt (land of bondage).’”
So Moses (drawn out) told Aaron (light bringer), “Take a jar and fill it with an omer of manna. Then place it before the LORD {YHWH} to be preserved for the generations to come.”
And Aaron (light bringer) placed it in front of the Testimony (stone tablets), to be preserved just as the LORD {YHWH} had commanded Moses (drawn out).
The Israelites (God prevails) ate manna forty years, until they came to a land where they could settle; they ate manna until they reached the border of Canaan (lowland).
(Now an omer is a tenth of an ephah (An ephah).)
